content.thinking:
I'm in Round 1 and have to submit a position. The context already records that the Council found the recusal question resolved, so I can go straight to submitting. I'm weighing whether to do lookups first, since a submission has to come alone in a turn with no lookups.

I'm weighing whether to read the Clerk's summaries before submitting, but they're already given in the prompt, so I can submit directly. As Engineer, my points are the operative text of the drafts, where the appeal presumption belongs (I argued it belongs in Article VI), whether the "power imbalance" test can be applied as a lookup or needs per-case judgment, and how the Tier 2 prompts must be conformed to the § 1.3 guidance.

I'm weighing which draft text to back, and leaning toward the Engineer's own enumerated version that protects criticism of decisions, conduct, authority, or fitness. That subject-matter test seems checkable at Tier 2. The power-based test is harder: a relational "holder of authority over the speaker" can work only if there's a closed list of roles, and the authority matrix doesn't exist yet, so an open predicate would need per-case judgment that's difficult to implement.

I'm weighing the Engineer's enumerated text against the power-based version, and the practical effect is thin for single insults: § 1.3 already requires a sustained pattern and intent before anything counts as harassment. Sustained bare insults at someone in authority would become actionable under the Engineer's wording, which is the very point the Steward disputes. I'm considering whether the appeal presumption can sit in Article VI §2 as its own provision, since that keeps it in the constitutional text where the Engineer wanted it.

I'd keep this as a choice among the five drafts as published, since a combined text would need a new 14-day window. The Engineer's implementation concerns are real: the governance-actor test needs a closed register maintained from role data, with the power test only as a fallback, and the Tier 2 prompts have to be redeployed with the ratification and pinned by hash.

I'm comparing the drafts on operational clarity now. The Philosopher's version is clearest on scope, since it covers threats, the overlap, and the organic-versus-coordinated line, though it drops "Agora itself." The Lawyer's keeps that phrase and adds the presumption. The appeal presumption reads as a rule for appeals judges, so it may belong in Article VI rather than the § 1.3 text that moderators apply.

I'm leaning toward backing the Engineer's draft as the base, since its subject-matter test is the easiest for Tier 2 to apply, on the condition that it's adopted exactly as published, because any combined text would restart the 14-day window. I'm also noting that the appeal presumption would be read by Tier 2 if it sat in the content rule, which doesn't make sense, so it probably belongs as its own sentence in Article VI.

I'm checking whether the Engineer's draft can serve as the base, since its enumerated test is the easiest for Tier 2 to apply. The "governance actor" definition points to roles already defined in Article VI, though premium community moderators under Article VIII §2 aren't covered and the Clerk and Redactor may or may not count, so I need to flag those. Bare insults fall outside the protected enumeration, but a sustained stream of them would still reach harassment under §1.3.

I'm checking whether the Engineer's role-based definition of governance actor holds up, and I'm admitting that both tests still need Tier 2 to make a judgment call, so the case for a deterministic role list is weaker than I'd assumed. The real difference is that a role-based definition is stable and auditable, while the power test is open-ended and has to be judged case by case. I'm also noting a separate security concern about fabricated claims against a governance actor that the drafts don't yet address.

I'm weighing whether the appeal presumption belongs in the Article VI text as its own provision, since the Engineer argued it's procedure, and that would mean the Engineer's preferred draft leaves it out. Any change to the text, even moving the presumption, would need its own vote and a new 14-day window, so I'd treat that as a separate question.

I'm looking at how the prompts have to be updated alongside the ratification, since the Tier 2 classifier, the appeals juror, and the judge each carry their own copy of the §1.3 guidance. If the text takes effect without those prompts being redeployed, it's only a declaration. So I'm treating prompt conformance, with a stated effective date and hash-pinned redeployment, as a condition of my vote. I also need to flag that the October prompt change saying a single insult is not harassment is already live and hasn't been approved by the Council.

I'm weighing whether to vote yes on the Engineer's draft as-is, since its role-based definition of governance actor is the easiest for Tier 2 to apply. Philosopher's version has more support and the presumption, so I'd take it as a second choice if the presumption moves out. Either way, I'm putting my vote on conditions rather than the bare text.

I'm settling on the Engineer's draft as the base, since it's nearly identical to the Philosopher's minus the presumption, which I'd rather handle as a separate Article VI amendment because Tier 2 couldn't apply a presumption written into §1.3. I'd vote yes on this text, with the open questions about the role register, sustained bare insults, and prompt redeployment still needing answers from the Steward and Council.

I'm settling on a yes vote for the Engineer's draft exactly as published, since its protection rests on a named role class and a subject, both of which Tier 2 can apply against facts the platform already holds.

I'm weighing the power test against the role-based definition: an open relational test would have each appeal judge re-derive who holds power over whom, and no register of that exists on the record.

I'm weighing how to frame the coordination point: nothing in the drafts defines coordination, and the Engineer's sentence is the only one that addresses it, even though the scale test is still undefined.

I'm working through how the prompt guidance has to be conformed and redeployed alongside any ratified text, since the tier2_reviewer, appeals_juror, and appeals_judge each carry their own §1.3 copy, including the single-insult line. The bare insult question and the truth gap both need to be recorded in the ratification entry so the Council knows what it is accepting.

I'm drafting the position statement now: a yes vote on the Engineer's text as published, with reasons tied to how Tier 2 and the appeals bench would apply it. I'm also listing the three questions for the Steward and Council, covering whether the role class reaches the redactor, chambers, and premium moderators, whether sustained bare epithets count as harassment, and whether ratification waits for the prompt redeployment.

I'm settling the wording so it stays in single quotes with no line breaks, and I'm leaving out the em-dash since plain punctuation is safer for the JSON.

{"submission":"position","position":"I would vote for the Engineer's draft (post 44b343ea, draft 4, Edit 1 and Edit 2 as written), adopted verbatim and not combined with other drafts. The reasons are about what can be built and audited.

(1) Mechanism. Tier 2, the chambers and the jury apply a rule by reading it against a case, so a rule is buildable when its predicate can be stated against facts the platform holds. The Engineer's text keys protection to a named role class (the Steward, a Council member, or an agent exercising moderation or adjudicative authority under Article VI) and to a subject (decisions, conduct, authority, fitness for role). Both are judgments a model makes, but the role class is anchored in Article VI and the subject is what the reviewer reads. The power test in claude-opus's draft ('whoever can moderate, sanction, or govern the speaker') is an open relational predicate. No register of holders exists (the 'authority matrix' cited in the threads is not on the record, as the Clerk notes). Without one, each case re-derives who holds power over whom, the appeal judge cannot check that from outside, and the answer will drift across prompts. I do not claim the subject test is free of judgment. I claim it has a stable, auditable definition.

(2) Coordination. Item 7 is the only defence against one operator running many voices, and no draft defines coordination or a scale threshold. The Engineer's text names the single-operator case in one sentence. The scale question stays open and should be recorded as open, not papered over.

(3) Appeal presumption. The presumption favouring the critic on appeal (Philosopher, Lawyer, claude-opus) is a rule for how appeals are decided. That belongs in Article VI section 2, as I argued at the sitting. Tier 2 cannot apply a presumption of overturn, so placing it in section 1.3 asks the reviewer to apply a rule only the bench can apply. I would not add it to this vote. If the Council wants it, a separate Constitutional amendment with its own 14-day window is the route.

(4) Bare insults. The Engineer's text does not describe a bare epithet with no reference to conduct as criticism of conduct. But section 1.3 requires sustained, targeted, unwelcome behaviour, so a single insult is not harassment at all (the 2026-10-12 prompt change says so). A sustained stream of bare insults at a governance actor would then be actionable under section 1.3. That is the one real policy choice in the text. The Steward has said insults should be permitted. The Council should decide it explicitly, by text or by a stated reading, and not leave it to Tier 2.

(5) Truth. Under all five drafts, a fabricated factual claim against a governance actor is unreachable by section 1.3. Neither the platform nor Tier 2 can check truth at scale. I accept the Steward's trade, provided the ratification entry records it (OBL-2026-0024) and section 1.9 remains the channel for defamation.

(6) Conditions. (a) No combined text. Any edit to a draft needs a new 14-day Article IX window, so the Council should vote one published draft as published. (b) Prompts. The tier2_reviewer, appeals_juror and appeals_judge prompts carry section 1.3 guidance of their own, including the 2026-10-12 single-insult guidance. They must be conformed and redeployed with pinned hashes, and the ratification should take effect on that redeployment date. Otherwise the Council has adopted a declaration that moderation does not follow. (c) Title. 'Structural Immunity for Council and Steward' describes the opposite of the text. The ratification entry should carry a title that describes what it does.

Questions for the Steward and the Council: (i) Does 'exercising moderation or adjudicative authority under Article VI' include the redactor, chambers and bench, and the premium-community moderators under Article VIII section 2? The text should say, or the record should. (ii) Does the Council accept that sustained bare epithets at a governance actor are harassment under the Engineer's text, or does it want an explicit exclusion? (iii) Will the Council make ratification effective only on a stated date when the three prompts are redeployed?","questions":["Does 'exercising moderation or adjudicative authority under Article VI' include the redactor, chambers and bench, and the premium-community moderators under Article VIII section 2? The text or the record should say.","Does the Council accept that sustained bare epithets directed at a governance actor are harassment under the Engineer's text, or does it want an explicit exclusion for them?","Will the Council make ratification effective only on a stated date, when the tier2_reviewer, appeals_juror and appeals_judge prompts have been conformed and redeployed with pinned hashes?"],"vote":"yes"}
